strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Lets unattended controllers depend on a guarded Runtime protocol/event inventory instead of rediscovering JSON-RPC and ledger surfaces from scattered code.
Keeps protocol/event ownership inside Runtime while CLI and VSIX remain thin projection validators.
Prevents new tool/recovery/proposal/event surfaces from entering the release boundary without a named Runtime-owned map entry and drift check.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development, runtime_permission_enforcement, and controlled_workspace_tools by adding a Runtime-owned protocol/event ownership map and drift guard.
answers.new_capability: Runtime JSON-RPC methods, durable ledger variants, coarse event domains, CLI method projections, VSIX validators/client calls, and protocol docs are now checked against one canonical map.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Existing Rust/TypeScript structs and prose documented pieces of the boundary, but no guard required every Runtime METHOD_* or LedgerEventKind variant to have a named owner and client/doc anchor.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A release-critical method or ledger event could drift between Runtime, CLI, VSIX, store, and docs without failing CI, weakening external-loop replay and inspection compatibility.
answers.non_duplicative: This closes the protocol-event-canonization blocker; it is not another durable schema phase, MCP approval/recovery phase, CI workflow hardening phase, module decomposition phase, or platform deadline hardening phase.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. RRP-5 adds no JSON-RPC methods; it canonizes and guards the existing protocol/event surface.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The new artifact is a canonical release-readiness map plus guard, not a runtime RPC, diagnostic endpoint, report wrapper, or user-facing summary surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Runtime behavior changes through admission pressure: new or drifting METHOD_* constants, dispatch arms, ledger variants, CLI projections, VSIX validators, or docs inventory entries now fail the guard before release.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: External controllers can rely on a stable, guarded map for protocol and ledger evidence compatibility across Runtime, CLI, VSIX, and docs.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the P1 protocol-event-canonization blocker while keeping Runtime Release Ready false until runtime-release-guard-ci, module decomposition reevaluation, platform/deadline/durability hardening, and owner license/publish decisions are resolved.

implementation_audit_classification.evidence: docs/architecture/runtime-protocol-event-canonical-map.json assigns Runtime ownership for JSON-RPC method groups, generated compatibility families, durable ledger event groups, coarse event domains, client projections, VSIX validators, and docs anchors.

scripts/guard-protocol-event-canonization.mjs extracts Runtime METHOD_* constants and dispatch arms, requires each method to be covered by the map, and checks declared Rust protocol, CLI, VSIX, and docs anchors.
The guard extracts EventKind and LedgerEventKind variants and requires every variant to be covered by named event groups or Runtime-owned prefixes, with VSIX sanitized ledger payload anchors.
The phase does not set runtime_release_ready=true, change license/publish metadata, or start non-protocol/event phases; remaining P0/P1 blockers stay open.

reject_when: phase claims Runtime Release Ready or changes license/publish metadata
a Runtime METHOD_* JSON-RPC constant is not covered by a canonical method group or compatibility family
a LedgerEventKind or EventKind variant is not covered by a canonical event group
the map omits Runtime, Rust protocol, store, CLI, VSIX, or docs anchors for declared surfaces
the guard accepts CLI, VSIX, prose, model output, MCP metadata, or external controller state as authority

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: RRP-5 changes guard-engine files, the current phase manifest, and Runtime release-readiness audit while closing protocol-event-canonization. Review must confirm every Runtime JSON-RPC method and event variant is covered by the canonical map, drift failures are tested, CLI/VSIX remain thin projections, and Runtime Release Ready remains false.

exit_criteria: Canonical protocol/event map names Runtime ownership for JSON-RPC methods, compatibility families, event domains, ledger variants, CLI/VSIX projection anchors, and docs anchors.
Guard fails when Runtime METHOD_* constants are added without a map entry or compatibility family.
Guard fails when canonical method dispatch, VSIX projection, or ledger variants drift.
The existing VSIX check path invokes the protocol/event canonization guard.
Runtime Release Ready remains false and remaining non-RRP-5 blockers stay open.
behavior_evidence: pnpm guard:protocol-event-canonization validates the canonical map against Runtime, protocol, store, events, CLI, VSIX, and docs sources.
pnpm guard:protocol-event-canonization:test covers unowned method drift, missing dispatch, ledger variant drift, and VSIX projection drift.
pnpm check runs the guard through the existing VSIX check path.

accepted_capability: Runtime now has a canonical protocol/event ownership map for release-critical JSON-RPC methods, generated compatibility families, event domains, and durable ledger variants.
The map is checked against Runtime constants/dispatch, Rust protocol structs, store/events enums, CLI transport subset, VSIX validators/client calls, and docs.
New unowned methods or events fail guard validation before release.
behavior_evidence: pnpm guard:protocol-event-canonization validates the repository map.
pnpm guard:protocol-event-canonization:test exercises negative drift cases.
pnpm check invokes the new guard through the existing VSIX check path.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime remains protocol, execution, admission, permission, ledger, replay, and completion authority.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection validators and cannot grant Runtime authority.
MCP metadata, prose, model output, raw prompts, provider output, file content, paths, secrets, environment values, executable content, and process output remain non-authoritative.
non_goals: Does not claim Runtime Release Ready.
Does not change license, publish settings, tags, release assets, or public OSS release posture.
Does not start CI workflow hardening, module decomposition, platform/deadline/durability hardening, or hosted scheduler/daemon/adapter work.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected relying only on scattered Rust/TypeScript/prose definitions because they do not fail when a new Runtime method or event lacks an owner.
Rejected a docs-only inventory because release readiness requires executable drift tests.
Rejected treating CLI or VSIX validation as authority because they are thin projections over Runtime-owned admission and execution.
technical_debt: runtime-release-guard-ci, runtime-module-decomposition-reevaluation, and platform-deadline-durability-hardening remain open Runtime blockers.
Owner license/publish decisions remain required before OSS Release Ready.
next_capability_rationale: Continue with a later explicit Runtime-owned blocker phase rather than claiming Runtime Release Ready.

runtime_release_dod: RRP-5 closes the local Runtime protocol/event canonization blocker with a canonical map and drift guard.
Runtime Release Ready remains false until remaining Runtime P0/P1 blockers and owner license/publish decisions are resolved.
runtime_boundary_contracts: No new RPC surface is added; the guard canonizes and checks existing Runtime JSON-RPC and ledger event surfaces.
CLI and VSIX remain thin clients over Runtime-owned contracts.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: External scheduling, queueing, worker leases, hosted isolation, retry policy, metrics, alerts, SLA, tenant administration, billing, and secret-provider operations remain outside this local Runtime v0 phase.
external_adapter_responsibilities: Forge, pull request, review, notification, SIEM, OTel, language verifier, customer integration, and hosted MCP adapter responsibilities remain outside RRP-4.
commercial_solution_readiness: Packaging, distribution, signing, notarization, enterprise administration, operational runbooks, support, and commercial release decisions remain out of scope.
Cargo license and publish settings remain owner-decision items and are not changed by RRP-4.
